rituals.name: GIVE THE BELIEF A POSTCODE
rituals.plain:
TRIGGER: Boundaries & over-responsibility
SUBPATTERN: Boundary confusion

PLAY TIME
about 4 minutes

GOAL
A rule can advise one neighbourhood without governing the entire world.

WHY THIS WORKS
Beliefs become rigid when a local lesson is promoted into universal law. Drawing its borders keeps useful learning while removing authority it never earned.

GAME MOVE
Give the belief four borders, prove one inside and outside case, then rewrite its lawful territory.

① NAME RULE — State the belief exactly, including words such as always, never, everyone, or nowhere.
② DRAW BORDERS — Draw four borders around it: WHERE, WHEN, FOR WHOM, and UNDER WHAT EVIDENCE might this rule actually apply?
③ TEST SCOPE — Find one real case inside those borders and one real case outside them. Do not argue; locate scope.
④ ISSUE POSTCODE — Rewrite the rule as: ‘This may apply when ___; it does not automatically govern ___.’

🏆 WIN
The belief ends with a supported jurisdiction instead of universal authority.

✨ REWARD
CONTROL RETURNED — Name Rule reached Issue Postcode; the change is recognisable and repeatable.

Name Rule → Draw Borders → Test Scope → Issue Postcode ↺ WIN
